messages.subject: Species accumulation curves
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
   I've been using camtrapR to manage my data from 18 camera stations I ran for a year. This package has been awesome for organizing, sorting, and removing duplicate captures (seriously, after manually sorting 100gb of images, this got the job done better and faster.)

I'm starting to work on some analyses, and wanted to know if there was an easy way to do species accumulation curves per station, and/or any community indices (ex. Shannon's diversity index). My stations were set up in 3 different habitat types, and I'm trying to compare communities among the habitats. I was thinking that for the accumulation curves, if there isn't a built in function the quickest route would be to pull the date of capture for each species from the meta data, then sort those and take the first one to build a dataframe of first day of capture for every species per camera station that I could then plot. However, if anyone has a better idea I would love to hear it.

Thanks for any help,
-Scott Martin

Hi all, thanks in advance for help with this question. I'm pretty new to R, so maybe this is a simple fix.

I'm trying to generate a record table from my camera trap images that are organized in a file system that is set up like this: stationID -> cameraID -> species folder -> raw images.

This is the code I am using:

LEVAS<- setwd("E:/CAMERAS/LF1")
exiftool_dir<-"E:/CAMERAS"
exiftoolPath(exiftoolDir = exiftool_dir)
LF1<-recordTable(inDir = LEVAS,
                 IDfrom = "directory",
                 cameraID = 'directory',
                 minDeltaTime = 0,
                 camerasIndependent = TRUE,
                 stationCol = "trap")

And I get this error message:

Warning: ArcGIS contains no images;  found 0 JPEGs
Classes : 2 images
Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "DateTimeOriginal", value = numeric(0)) :
  replacement has 0 rows, data has 2

I don't understand why it's looking in Arc, that file system isn't even on the hard drive I am directing it to. Thoughts? Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: Species accumulation curves
messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,
you are right, there is no built-in function to give you species accumulation curves. I would do the accumulation curves just the way you suggested. Here's some code that might work for you (it requires the DateTimeOriginal column to be in POSIXct format.

data(recordTableSample)
subset_specaccum <- aggregate(x = recordTableSample$DateTimeOriginal,
                              by = list(recordTableSample$Station,
                                        recordTableSample$Species),
                              FUN = min)

Best regards,
Jürgen

Hi Tara,
I'm sorry for the confusing error message. I suppose what happens is that the inDir is specified incorrectly, but I'm not sure. Is LF1 a camera trap station? If so, then inDir is specified incorrectly. inDir must point to the directory that contains all the station folders.

Here's a suggestion for how to write the code (assuming your station folders are in E:/CAMERAS

exiftool_dir<-"E:/CAMERAS"  # so exiftool.exe is in E:/CAMERAS?
exiftoolPath(exiftoolDir = exiftool_dir)  # again, only needed if exiftool.exe ist not in e.g. C:/Windows

LEVAS<- "E:/CAMERAS/LF1"   # setwd() is not needed

LF1<-recordTable(inDir = LEVAS,
                 IDfrom = "directory",
                 cameraID = 'directory',
                 minDeltaTime = 0,
                 camerasIndependent = TRUE,

                 stationCol = "trap")

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: How to remove dependent events when using my own manually created recordTableSample?
messages.subject_clean: How to remove dependent events when using my own manually created recordTableSample?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Meryl,
currently there is no built-in function to do this for you. It may be a helpful feature though for future releases of the package. Thank you for the suggestion.
Here is some code you can use in the meantime:

# try this with the sample record table
data(recordTableSample)

# split it into separate data frames for each station/species combination
recs_split <- split(x = recordTableSample,
                    f = list(recordTableSample$Station,
                             recordTableSample$Species),
                    drop = TRUE)

# calculate time intervals between subsequent records within these data frames and save as new column "difftime"
rec.df.list <- lapply(recs_split, FUN = function(x){
  x <- x[order(x$DateTimeOriginal),]
  difftime_tmp <- diff(x$DateTimeOriginal)
  units(difftime_tmp) <- "secs"
  x$difftime <- c(NA, difftime_tmp)
  return(x)
  }
  )

# reassemble into 1 data frame
recordTableSample2 <- do.call("rbind", rec.df.list)

# remove records within 60 minutes of one another (3600 seconds or NA if it was the first record of a species at a station)
recordTableSample2a <- recordTableSample2[recordTableSample2$difftime >= 3600 |
                                          is.na <http://is.na>(recordTableSample2$difftime),]

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject_clean: Problem to run a Report Survey
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eduardo,
two possible reasons come to mind: 1) you have species with one record only, or 2) there is species with very few records which happen to fall into almost exactly the same time of day. In both cases, the estimation of the bandwidth for the kernel density estimation for the activity density plots will fail.
You can check with
table(PMRData_survey5$specie)

Good news is that this will be fixed in the next release of the package (I changed the code already).
Best,
Jürgen
